text:
maya: Quick question — for Redwood Private SDK deployments: what's our recommended pattern for providing cloud KMS credentials to the runtime? env vars, HashiCorp Vault, or cloud secret managers? Trying to write a short guidance blurb for the infra docs.

alex: Short answer: no long-lived static creds in env vars if you can avoid it. Prefer cloud-native identity (IAM role / Workload Identity / Managed Identity) + short-lived tokens. Use Vault or the cloud secret manager as an additional layer when you need secret rotation/consent. :+1:

sanjay: For AWS specifically: prefer EC2/EKS IAM role + IRSA for pods. Give the role only kms:Encrypt/kms:Decrypt + kms:GenerateDataKey when doing envelope encryption. If an app needs to create keys, separate admin role. Avoid embedding AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/SECRET in envs.

kevin: For GCP/Azure: same story. Use Workload Identity for GKE and Managed Identity on AKS/VMs. Short-lived access via token exchange — no static keyfile checked into containers.

maya: Great. How do we phrase envelope encryption guidance? People get confused about where DEKs live and how rotation works.

kevin: Practical pattern: app calls KMS GenerateDataKey (or equivalent) -> gets plaintext DEK + encrypted DEK blob. Use plaintext DEK in-memory to encrypt payload, persist only the encrypted DEK alongside ciphertext. Never persist plaintext DEKs to disk.

alex: Add: keep DEKs scoped to record/object when possible, reuse only if you have strong caching/TTL. Use an envelope format with metadata: kms_key_alias, kms_ciphertext_blob, algorithm, version. That makes rotation and audit easier.

sanjay: Rotation notes: there are two distinct things — "rotate key material for the same CMK" vs "create a new CMK and rewrap." AWS KMS automatic rotation rotates material for the same key id (no rewrap needed). If you create a new CMK and point alias to it, you WILL need a rewrap/rewrap-job to re-encrypt stored DEKs. Recommend: prefer key material rotation when possible; if alias swap is required, schedule a controlled rewrap job and add a fallback to use legacy ciphertext during transition.

maya: Helpful. Any minimal IAM example we can paste in docs?

alex: Paste this small policy for service role that only needs GenerateDataKey + Decrypt/Encrypt + DescribeKey:

```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "kms:Encrypt",
        "kms:Decrypt",
        "kms:GenerateDataKey",
        "kms:DescribeKey"
      ],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/REDACTED"
    }
  ]
}
```

kevin: Also consider KMS grants for short-term operations if you need to delegate without changing policy. Grants can be revoked quickly.

maya: Ops questions: where do we store the config that points to the KMS alias or secret path? env var vs Vault path?

sanjay: store the reference (alias, secret path, key id) in the service config (kubernetes Secret / env) but keep the credentials/keys themselves behind identity. Example: set env var KMS_KEY_ALIAS=alias/redwood-prod and let workload identity handle auth. If you must store cloud credentials, keep them in Vault/SSM and mount as volume with short TTL tokens.

alex: For SDKs we ship, default behavior should be: 1) attempt workload identity; 2) fallback to cloud secret manager; 3) last resort, read env var. Document the order clearly and show examples for AWS/GCP/Azure.

maya: Audit logging + RBAC: anything to call out? We need a one-paragraph checklist.

kevin: Checklist bullets (short): CloudTrail / Cloud Audit Logs enabled for KMS calls; ensure log export to central SIEM; restrict who can manage key policy/aliases; use service account separation (no shared admin keys); enable key usage metrics & alarms for unusual decrypt rates.

sanjay: Also record KMS key id/alias in the application logs (not the plaintext keys) so we can map decrypts to key. And include DEK rotation events in audit trail.

maya: Incident playbook for suspected key compromise?

alex: Quick playbook we can include: 1) Rotate affected CMK (or disable if possible), 2) Revoke any outstanding grants, 3) Block/rotate service roles/identities if needed, 4) Kick off rewrap job for DEKs if we moved to a new CMK, 5) Notify legal/compliance, 6) Open incident ticket + timeline, 7) Increase logging retention for related artifacts.

kevin: Add step to snapshot current ciphertexts & metadata before mass rewrap so we can rollback if rewrap job misbehaves.

maya: Perfect. I'll draft a short doc with these patterns and examples. One ask: can infra add example for IRSA + KMS permissions and a Vault-to-KMS example? infra-bot: queued ticket #INC-1423 to add examples to infra repo.

maya: Thanks all — I'll post the doc draft in #docs-devex once it's ready. :pray:
